rulings.Case Title: IN THE MATTER OF THE RAYMOND C. LOW AND IRENE C. LOW REVOCABLE TRUST DATED JULY 6, 2001
rulings.Calendar Matter: Petitioners Notice And First Motion To Compel Production Of Documents From Respondent Gary Low And For Monetary Sanctions
rulings.Rulings: This tentative ruling is issued by Judge Russell S. Roeca. Before the court is Petitioner's First Motion to Compel Production of Documents from Respondent Gary Low and for Monetary Sanctions ("Motion"). Per the Notice of Motion, Petitioner seeks to compel production of documents in response to Petitioner's First Set of Requests for Production of Documents ("RFPs"), pursuant to Code of Civil Procedure section 2031 et seq., and for monetary sanctions in the amount of $7,722 pursuant to Code of Civil Procedure section 2031.310(h). Per the Separate Statement, at issue is production of documents responsive to RFPs No. 119, 121, 134, 138, 151, 155, 156. Per the Separate Statement, and the declaration of attorney Jessica I. Neugebauer (par. 21 and Ex. M), on February 21, 2025, Respondent served Second Amended Responses to Requests for Production of Documents, Set One. The response to each of the RFPs now at issue was, "Responding Party will produce the documents responsive to this request that are in the possession, custody, or control of the Responding Party." Prior iterations of Respondent's responses had contained objections to the RFPs now at issue; counsel met and conferred telephonically on the objections; supplemental responses and a privilege log were produced (see, Decl. of Neugebauer, par. 4, 8, 11, 16, 17, 18, 21, 22, Ex. E, I, J, M). The February 21, 2025, Second Amended Responses to Requests for Production of Documents, Set One did not pose objections to the RFPs now at issue. The responsive financial documents produced contain redactions apparently done, initially, by Respondent Gary Low himself, without aid of counsel, and later supplemented by counsel. Some of these redactions were later corrected by his counsel as erroneous (Decl. of Neugebauer at par. 25; Decl. of Fargo-Matsuda at par. 15). The parties and this Court conducted an Informal Discovery Conference on March 20, 2026, in part about production in response to the RFPs now at issue. The Motion is GRANTED (see, Code of Civil Procedure sections 2031.210, 2031.280). Respondent Gary Low is ordered to produce the documents responsive to Petitioner's First Set of Requests for Production of Documents, No. 119, 121, 134, 138, 151, 155, 156, that are in his possession, custody, or control, in their unredacted form. Parties shall comply with this court's May 16, 2023 Protective Order - Confidential Designation regarding these documents. The Motion's request for sanctions pursuant to Code of Civil Procedure section 2031.310(h) is GRANTED. Respondent Gary Low unsuccessfully opposed this Motion, and the court does not find that he acted with substantial justification or that other circumstances make the imposition of the sanction unjust. Respondent Gary Low shall pay Petitioner Joseph Wu $5,880 in sanctions, within 30 days of entry of this Order. Any party wishing to contest this tentative ruling by appearing at the scheduled hearing must do so advise other parties and the courtroom clerk (415-551-3702) no later than 4:00 p.m. on the day before the hearing. To appear by Zoom, go to zoom.us and click "Join Meeting." Enter Meeting ID number 1602254765 and passcode 514879. To appear telephonically through Zoom, call 1-669-900-6833 and follow the prompts. Enter Meeting ID number 1602254765# and passcode 514879#. Parties appearing via Zoom should use their full names in the "Your Name" section. Counsel and parties may appear by audio-only telephone through CourtCall by calling CourtCall at 1-888-882-6878 and obtaining an appearance access code for the hearing's scheduled date and time in Department 204.

rulings.Case Title: IN THE MATTER OF THE RAYMOND C. LOW AND IRENE C. LOW REVOCABLE TRUST DATED JULY 6, 2001
rulings.Calendar Matter: Notice And Motion To Compel Respondent Gary Low To Appear For Deposition And For Monetary Sanctions
rulings.Rulings: [Part 1 of 3] This tentative ruling is issued by Judge Russell S. Roeca. Before the court is Petitioners' Motion to Compel Respondent Gary Low to Appear for Deposition; Request For Monetary Sanctions ("Motion"). On July 30, 2026, Respondent filed an Opposition to the Petitioner's Motion. Petitioner's Motion is DENIED in part and GRANTED in part, as follows. Pursuant to Cal. Code of Civil Proc. sec. 2025.450(a), "If, after service of a deposition notice, a party to the action [] without having served a valid objection under section 2025.410, fails to appear for examination, or to proceed with it [] the party giving the notice may move for an order compelling the deponent's attendance and testimony[.]" A motion under subdivision (a) shall: (1) set forth specific facts showing good cause justifying the production for inspection of any document; (2) be accompanied by a meet and confer declaration under section 2016.040, or, when the deponent fails to attend the deposition and produce the documents, by a declaration stating that the petitioner has contacted the deponent to inquire about the nonappearance. (Code of Civil Procedure sec. 2025.450(a).) A meet and confer declaration in support of a motion brought under Cal. Code of Civil Proc. sec. 2025.450 (a) shall state facts showing a reasonable and good faith attempt, either in person, by telephone, or by video conference, to informally resolve each issue presented by the motion. (Code of Civil Procedure sec. 2016.040(a).) The deposition notice does not seek production of documents for inspection. (Decl. of Fargo-Masuda, Exh. W.) The Declaration of Christopher Fargo-Masuda in support of the Motion details the seven deposition notices served on Respondent Gary Low, from the initial deposition date of October 23, 2024, through the deposition notice for June 22, 2026 at issue in this Motion, and counsels' communications around the three mutual postponements and the seven unilateral cancelations of the noticed depositions. Although counsel communicated in various ways, including telephonically, over this period of time, the record before the Court does not show Movant met and conferred in person, telephonically, or by video conference, to resolve each issue presented in this Motion regarding the June 22, 2026 noticed deposition, before resorting to the court's intervention. Counsel's declaration in support of the Motion lists only one phone call with opposing counsel, Erin Norcia, on June 15 (par. 33, 37); it is not characterized as a meet and confer effort regarding the June 22 noticed deposition - Mr. Fargo-Masuda was calling regarding a joint status report. However, it resulted in Ms. Norcia telling Mr. Fargo-Masuda that Gary Low would not attend the June 22 deposition. That phone call was followed on June 16 by Gary Low's written objections to the noticed deposition, on grounds that: (1) the notice of deposition was untimely; (2) Gary Low's doctor advised against his sitting for a deposition; and (3) Gary Low's counsel was going to be unavailable the date of the deposition. Counsel then exchanged further emails, but apparently did not thereafter meet and confer in person, telephonically, or over video-conference before the Motion was filed on June 29. Failure to meet and confer in accordance with statute means that the Motion does not comply with the statutory requirements of a motion to compel a deponent's attendance and testimony at a deposition (Code of Civil Procedure sec. 2025.450(a)). The Motion is DENIED as procedurally deficient.

rulings.Rulings: [Part 3 of 3] The Motion's request for monetary sanctions pursuant to Civ. Proc Code sec. 2023.030(a) and Civ. Proc. Code sec. 2025.450 (a) and (g)(1) in the amount of $13,600 from Respondent Gary Low is DENIED. While the Court acknowledges that Petitioner has had to reschedule depositions on multiple occasions, Mr. Low either provided advance notice of his inability to appear or the parties mutually agreed to postpone the deposition. The court does not find, on this record, that this conduct constitutes misuse of the discovery process warranting monetary sanctions. rulings.Case Title: IN THE MATTER OF THE RAYMOND C. LOW AND IRENE C. LOW REVOCABLE TRUST DATED JULY 6, 2001
rulings.Calendar Matter: ADDED TO CALENDAR FOR For The Purposes Of Posting The Tentative Ruling
rulings.Rulings: [Part 2 of 3] Nevertheless, the Court, for good cause shown, may make any order that justice requires to protect any party, deponent, or other natural person or organization from unwarranted annoyance, embarrassment, or oppression, or undue burden and expense (See Code of Civil Procedure sec. 2025.420). Per the declarations of counsel and Mr. Low, the sixth noticed deposition of Mr. Low (May 21, 2026) was not conducted because Mr. Low was advised by his doctor to not sit for a deposition; the parties have not been able to agree on a deposition date since (Decl. of Norcia at par. 13-18; Decl. of Fargo-Masuda at par. 23-36). Mr. Gary Low is the Respondent in this matter. It is reasonable for him to be deposed by Petitioner in this matter. Respondent's testimony cannot be made available to one party while withheld from another. The court seeks to balance Gary Low's asserted health risks with Petitioner's right to obtain discovery in this matter. Insofar as the parties appear to agree in their email communications exchanged since May 2026, and in the papers now before the court, that there should be some form of certain medical accommodations for Respondent's deposition, the court exercises its discretion to make any order that protects any party from abuse of discovery and ORDERS as follows: 1. Gary Low shall appear for deposition on a date ordered by the Court (Code of Civil Procedure sec. 2025.420. Mr. Low's declaration signed under penalty of perjury states that his physician advised against participation in depositions and court proceedings while he undergoes medical evaluation and treatment, at least through August 15, 2026. Counsel shall meet and confer in person, telephonically, or over video conference within the next ten days after issuance of this Order to determine deposition dates for Respondent. An initial deposition date for Respondent shall be scheduled and noticed for any mutually-available date within the next forty-five days. 2. Pursuant to Cal. Civ. Proc Code sec. 2025.290(a), a deposition is generally limited to seven hours. If Respondent is unable to complete the scheduled deposition in a single day because of his asserted medical condition, the deposition shall be suspended and continued to the next mutually-available date. 3. Respondent may take reasonable breaks during the deposition, as needed, as long as there is no question pending when the break begins. The break shall last no more than 30 minutes. After 30 minutes, the deposition officer may suspend the session, at which point counsel shall continue the deposition to the next mutually-available date. 4. If Respondent undergoes further medical evaluation and it is determined by his treating physician that he cannot safely proceed with a scheduled deposition, counsel for Respondent shall inform counsel for Petitioner of this information as soon as reasonably practicable to do so, and in no instance less than 36 hours before the scheduled deposition. Counsel shall thereafter reschedule the deposition to the next mutually-available date available under the treating physician's orders. 5. Counsel shall meet and confer in person, telephonically, or over video conference to mutually determine the duration, format, breaks, and any other medical accommodations necessary for the deposition to take place, if not otherwise addressed in this Order.

rulings.Case Title: THE ESTATE OF TERESA DE LAURETIS
rulings.Calendar Matter: PETITION FOR LETTERS OF ADMINISTRATION WITH WILL ANNEXED
rulings.Rulings: Hearing for the sole purpose of admitting the will dated 9/15/21 (although the attorney's name was misspelled in the published notice). No appearance is required. Status hearing will be set on 2/8/28 for closing the estate. If a petition for final distribution or a report of status with a petition requesting additional time for estate administration is filed at least two weeks before that status hearing date, no appearance will be required on that date. (Issues raised by the court should be addressed in a supplement or amendment that stands on its own and simply provides the missing or correct information, not in response to "examiner's notes," which are not part of the record.) If a will has not been filed, it should just be filed; there is no need to explain in a pleading that it will be filed.

rulings.Case Title: THE ESTATE OF WILLIAM WOOLF
rulings.Calendar Matter: PETITION FOR LETTERS OF ADMINISTRATION WITH WILL ANNEXED
rulings.Rulings: Continued to 09/23/2026. Issues necessitating continuance: 1)The original will has not been lodged with the court (Probate Code Section 8200(a)(1)). 2) Please explain why an estate this size (approximately $25,000) requires a formal probate, as opposed to being distributed pursuant to Probate Code Section 13100. 3) The date of death must be specified for all deceased devisees and heirs (LRSF 14.18.D.1). Please indicate the date of death for Morton Capp and Gene Woolf. 4) A written renunciation must be filed by or on behalf of a nominated executor who does not desire to act (LRSF 14.24). 5) Please describe the efforts to locate Ian Hawkins, Ronnie Mellon, and Danny Owen. They are beneficiaries of decedent's will and entitled to notice of the petition. 6) No Confidential Statement of Birth Date and Driver's License Number (Form DE-147S) has been filed (San Francisco Local Rule 14.18.E). 7) All notices must include language about remote appearances (San Francisco Local Rule 14.1.C.6)). 8) No proposed order has been received or lodged with the court (LSRF 14.7.A). Please address the above issues and deliver courtesy copies of all further filings to this examiner no later than 09/09/2026 to avoid additional continuance.
